issues.finding: The context definition only constrains variables free in the whole term. Conflicting unused assignments can reappear below a binder, and extending the context with a binder of the same name can create conflicting types.
issues.proposed_resolution: Require at most one formula per variable throughout the context and rename bound variables fresh for the context before recursive typing.

issues.finding: The clause assumes N has type A but types an injection from the undeclared formula-style placeholder !M.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use N as the injection's payload term.

issues.finding: The branch contexts refer to x and y while the displayed case term binds x1 and x2.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use x1 and x2 in the two branch contexts, matching the actual case binders.

issues.finding: The proposition asserts a type exists for every raw proof term, although the same section gives an untypable self-application abstraction. The opening uniqueness sentence also presupposes a corresponding typing proof without a well-typed condition.
issues.proposed_resolution: State at-most-one type for arbitrary terms and exactly one for well-typed terms; qualify the opening typing-proof assertion to well-typed terms.

issues.finding: The reference following the definition of tN3i points to the N2i table, duplicating the label issue corrected at OLP-0693.
issues.proposed_resolution: Point to tab:tN3ip, the distinct label already applied to rules-tN3.

translation_treatment: Translate the entire type section with globally consistent contexts, fresh binders, corrected injection and branch names, partial type uniqueness and the unique N3i table reference. Frozen English is untouched.
